rows.verified: Biological agents are microorganisms or other agents capable of causing infection, allergy, toxicity or another human-health hazard.
Workplace biological agents include bacteria, fungi, viruses and parasites.
Proteins associated with transmissible spongiform encephalopathies are also covered as biological agents.
Some biological agents are zoonotic and can pass from animals to humans.
COSHH is the main legislation used to control workplace exposure to biological agents.
Incidental exposure can arise through blood, body fluids, contaminated water or waste material.
Deliberate work includes planned handling, propagation, processing or manipulation of biological agents.
Biological-agent classification considers infectivity, disease severity, community spread and availability of vaccines or treatment.
Biological-agent risk depends on agent classification, exposure route, concentration, task, containment, controls and worker susceptibility.
HSE biological-agent evidence is agent-, workplace-, task-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Compressed-air hazards include bodily entry through an orifice, skin penetration, explosions and eye damage from particles.
Overpressurisation is a major compressed-air hazard.
Blockages and failure of automatic controls can contribute to dangerous overpressure.
Overspeeding, nearby fires, overheating and deposit accumulation are recognised compressed-air risk factors.
HSE guidance covers compressor plant, air receivers, dryers and coolers.
Main-line systems, actuators, portable pneumatics and pneumatic machinery are included in the guidance scope.
Inspection, maintenance and training are core compressed-air safety controls.
The guidance is intended for compressor designers, manufacturers, installers and users.
Compressed-air risk depends on pressure, equipment condition, controls, blockage, maintenance, task and operator competence.
HSE compressed-air evidence is equipment-, system-, task-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
